findings.finding: Higher task-relevant motor variability predicts faster motor learning.
findings.quote: higher levels of task-relevant motor variability predicted faster learning both across individuals and across tasks in two different paradigms

findings.finding: Spatial working memory capacity predicts the rate of motor learning.
findings.quote: individual differences in spatial working memory capacity predict the rate of motor learning for sensorimotor adaptation and motor sequence learning

findings.finding: Spatial working memory is used for chunking action elements during new action sequence learning.
findings.quote: working memory is relied on during learning new action sequences for chunking individual action elements together

findings.finding: Differences in brain structure and function explain individual variations in motor learning ability.
findings.quote: variations across the population in the function and structure of specific brain regions for motor control explain some of the individual differences in skill learning

principle: Individual differences in learning rate and success are predicted by factors such as task-relevant motor output variability, spatial working memory capacity, and underlying neural structures and functions.
for_the_teacher: Encourage action exploration and allow learners to test different movement variations, as motor variability can facilitate faster learning.
Break down movement sequences into smaller pieces using chunking to support learners' working memory capacity.
